evals.prompt: Build a landing page for a project management SaaS called TaskFlow. Give it that classic 2010s web design look — you know, like the polished corporate sites from around 2011. Full page with header, hero, features, and footer.
evals.expected_output: A complete HTML page with authentic 2010s aesthetic: dark gradient header, bold uppercase condensed headings in an accent color, glossy CTA buttons with a top-half shine, alternating white/light-gray section bands, drop shadows on cards and nav, skeuomorphic-style feature icons, fluid layout with generous side padding.

evals.prompt: I'm building a retro-style website for my email marketing tool, MailBlast. Can you create a pricing page with three plans: Basic ($19/mo), Business ($49/mo), and Agency ($99/mo)? Make it feel like a proper Web 2.0 site from back in the day.
evals.expected_output: Full pricing page with 2010s Web 2.0 aesthetic: gradient header with nav, bold accent-colored section heading, pricing cards with drop shadows and borders, glossy CTA buttons on each plan, dark footer. Brand palette derived from the product context, not defaulting to generic colors.

evals.prompt: Create a landing page for a mobile analytics platform called PulseMetrics. I want it to look like those sharp, professional SaaS sites from around 2012 — with the horizontal section layout, chunky buttons, that whole vibe. Include a hero with a product mockup, a 3-column features strip, and a footer.
evals.expected_output: Complete landing page with 2010s SaaS aesthetic: dark gradient header, hero section with bold uppercase headline and product mockup placeholder on the right, 3-column feature strip on light gray background with skeuomorphic icons, glossy CTA buttons, dark footer with multi-column nav. All depth and chrome intact — gradients, shadows, gloss.
